title: _current_weather books forecast row 0's wind as current at any age; the N-no-expiry barrier cannot see an index-0 read
claim: During a weather-fetch outage of 1 to 72 h, HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._current_weather returns the wind of the held forecast's first row, not the row covering now (or none past the horizon), at all 72 of 72 hours. At 30 h the diagnosis record books 10.0 m/s where the covering row says 40.0. The fixed sibling forecast_outdoor_now, over the same rows, mismatches at 0 of 72 hours.
mechanism: _current_weather reads self._weather_forecast[0] with no timestamp match and no end bound. The forecast is kept verbatim when a fetch fails or returns empty: _fetch_weather keeps the previous list and only marks _weather_stale_since, and no learner freezes on that. So once the source stops updating, the row booked as 'now' drifts back by the outage length. It feeds the house and lower-floor loss replay (_replay_interval -> _replay_step's weather argument) and the #52 diagnosis capture's planned.wind_speed. forecast_outdoor_now's own docstring names this exact assumption as wrong ('Assuming entry 0 is the current hour ... a stale forecast ... reads hours out of phase'), and #2229 fixed that sibling with _covering_index. The class barrier, tests/entities.py's _r10_covering_lookups, counts only the AST shape `bisect_right(...) - 1`, so a lookup that indexes [0] or walks a loop is invisible to it.

evidence.unit: outage hours (of 72) at which _current_weather's wind is not the covering row's
evidence.contention_note: shared compute box; count is contention-immune

perturbation.change: swap _current_weather in memory for the same body indexed by coordinator._covering_index over the rows' own timestamps (harness --perturb covering)

metric_definition: Hours H in 1..72 after the last good hourly fetch at which _current_weather()[0] differs from the wind of the row _covering_index picks at now (0 when none covers).
phenomenon_property: Every read of a time-indexed series as 'the value now' selects the row covering now with an end bound, and yields nothing past it. A positional read such as entry [0] or [-1], or a loop that falls through to the last row, is a covering lookup too and goes through _covering_index.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s2/covering_census.py   (lists every read of a forecast/series container by constant index [0]/[-1] and every loop fall-through to the last element in the package, beside the barrier's bisect_right count)

null_control.value: h0_match=1 (fresh fetch: row 0 covers now); outdoor_sibling_mismatch_hours=0 of 72
null_control.note: The effect needs an outage. The bounded sibling over the same rows shows the rows and clock are honest.

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._current_weather: match now by row timestamp through _covering_index, as forecast_outdoor_now does, and return the no-wind default past the horizon. Barrier: widen tests/entities.py's _r10_covering_lookups beyond the bisect_right shape to constant-index reads of a timed series attribute (_weather_forecast, _solar_radiation_forecast, price lists), with a reasoned list.
